An authenticated repository collaborator with Admin access can escalate their effective permission to Owner by submitting `mode=4` to the collaboration access-mode endpoint.

After the escalation, the collaborator can perform Owner-only operations, including transferring the repository to their own account.

Confirmed on Gitea 1.27.1.

### Details

The web handler passes the submitted `uid` and `mode` directly to `ChangeCollaborationAccessMode`:

https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/blob/v1.27.1/routers/web/repo/setting/collaboration.go#L111-L116

The model accepts permission values up to and including `AccessModeOwner`:

https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/blob/v1.27.1/models/repo/collaboration.go#L103-L132

The relevant validation is:

```go
if mode <= perm.AccessModeNone || mode > perm.AccessModeOwner {
    return nil
}
```

Because only values greater than `AccessModeOwner` are rejected, `mode=4` is accepted and written to both `collaboration.mode` and the effective `access.mode`.

Owner checks rely on this effective access mode:

[https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/blob/v1.27.1/models/perm/access/repo_permission.go#L35-L38](https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/blob/v1.27.1/models/perm/access/repo_permission.go#L35-L38)

### Impact

This is an authenticated privilege-escalation vulnerability.

Any user who has been granted Admin collaborator access to a repository can obtain effective Owner permissions and perform operations that should be restricted to the repository owner. The demonstrated impact is takeover of a private repository by transferring it to the attacker's account.
